name: Sovereign democracy
summary: Sovereign democracy is the Kremlin ideology coined by Vladislav Surkov in 2006. It holds that Russia's political life must be elected and directed solely by the Russian nation, free of outside control or judgement, with a leading state, a dominant party and managed institutions, and state control of strategic sectors. It rejects both Western tutelage and ethnic isolationism and is hostile to oligarchic and bureaucratic capture of the state.
scope: The concept as formulated by Vladislav Surkov in his February 2006 United Russia speech and November 2006 Ekspert article, as used by United Russia, Nashi and Putin-era officials in 2006-2008. It excludes later Putin-era conservative doctrines except where the sources link them; many social questions are therefore low-confidence inferences.

sources.usedFor: Surkov quotes tying sovereignty to the army and navy and calling for a national ideology.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Surkov names impoverished hospitals and schools as unfinished state business, so a state-guaranteed system fits; he sets out no healthcare model, so this is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The stated aim is material welfare and justice for every person in Russia, which leans toward higher pay floors, but no wage policy is stated.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Surkov held that without genuine state management of the economy there is no growth, and he wanted the state in vital sectors, so he does not give markets priority.

public-ownership.rationale: Surkov's outline calls for state control of vital sectors such as pipelines, the electricity grid and railroads.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Sources say nothing on tax rates; hostility to oligarchs pulls one way and elite alliances the other.

unions-good.rationale: The managed public sphere leaves little room for independent organisations; unions are never discussed, so this is inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Strategic sectors are to be under state control and oligarchs are to be sidelined, so property yields to national interest; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Surkov warns of an oligarchic coup reducing Russia to a raw-materials appendage of transnational firms, implying firmer state control of business.

cut-welfare.rationale: Surkov treats poor hospitals and schools as a failing to repair, not a bill to cut; no welfare-cutting case appears.

worker-ownership.rationale: The state-led, corporatist outlook gives no role to worker cooperatives; inferred from the statist economy.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Sovereignty is framed in military-police terms and the state manages the public sphere, so security surveillance fits; not discussed directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Never addressed; state-centred conservatism of the Putin era implies prohibition.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Surkov attacks promoters of ethnic isolation as charlatans and the state shapes the public sphere; speech law itself is not discussed.

strong-leader.rationale: The concept stresses a leading role for the state and the dominant party around Putin, and Surkov offered "people's autocracy" as a gloss.

state-harmful.rationale: Sovereign democracy is built on the society-forming and leading role of the state, the opposite of this claim.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; a state-order orientation implies tight control of arms.

empower-police-military.rationale: Surkov linked sovereignty to the army and navy and wanted restored power abroad, which implies strengthening the security forces.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; the conservative state-order outlook implies keeping it illegal.

decide-locally.rationale: Sakwa cites Surkov's view that Russian mentality strives for political wholeness and centralised power.

rehabilitation.rationale: The sources say nothing on penal policy and adherents would be split.

traditional-family.rationale: Not in the 2006 texts; the movement later allied with the Church and conservative values, so this is inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed by Surkov; the later conservative alignment of the regime implies opposition.

abortion-legal.rationale: Never addressed; abortion remained legal under the regime while the Church pressed against it, so adherents are split.

more-religion-public.rationale: Archbishop Kirill backed the concept and rejected Western democratic values, implying a larger public role for religion; inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; a nation-first outlook gives no priority to race-based remedies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; implied by the conservative cultural line.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Sakwa notes the claim that democratic forms reflect a country's own traditions, culture and psychology.

gradual-change.rationale: The concept presents the state as guardian against a bureaucratic or oligarchic coup and against a return to the disorder of the 1990s.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Surkov frames Russia as multiethnic and rejects ethnic isolation, yet says nothing on immigration levels.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The outline centres on Moscow's right to limit the influence of international law, global economic bodies and world opinion on its affairs.

free-trade.rationale: Surkov wants to move beyond a raw-materials economy and keep vital sectors under state control; no trade policy is stated, so inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Sovereignty means Russian national interests are directed by the Russian nation, though Surkov also seeks partnership with friendly Western governments.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Putin, cited in the sources, is categorically against political tools used to intervene in internal affairs, which implies rejecting rights-based intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Sovereignty as a defining value implies firm borders; Surkov's multiethnic nation is not an open-borders case.

limit-growth.rationale: Surkov's stress on competitiveness and on an intellectual economy implies growth is wanted.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; a resource-export state with sovereignty priorities implies resisting external demands.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Surkov calls for converting the raw-materials economy into an intellectual one and building an innovation culture; no sweeping claim is made.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; implied by energy-sovereignty and state technological ambition.

revolution-justified.rationale: The concept casts the state as guardian against coups and upheaval; revolution is treated as a threat.

experts-over-public.rationale: Surkov holds that all democracies are managed, which implies elite guidance of policy over raw public preference.

central-planning.rationale: Surkov wants state control of vital sectors but also an intellectual, innovation-driven economy, not full planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; state-run strategic sectors sit beside private markets in practice.

land-value-tax.rationale: No source discusses land taxation; a state-led budget built on resource rents suggests no single-tax scheme, so this is an inference.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not discussed; the elite-aligned system is unlikely to favour heavy inheritance taxes, inferred from its alliance with business elites.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; the welfare aim is justice through state-led growth rather than unconditional transfers.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Defence of national economic sovereignty and state control of vital sectors implies protection; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Surkov argued that without genuine state management of the economy there will be no growth and wanted state control of vital sectors.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Surkov's concern is oligarchic capture and state control of strategic sectors, not a programme of small owners; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nothing in the concept questions money or wage labour; it sits within a market economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; a strong-state outlook opposes abolishing monetary institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The concept has a leading, society-forming state role and a managed public sphere, which fits state-recognised bodies; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: United Russia became a dominant party within a formally multiparty system; adherents claim democracy and do not call for one party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; adherents claim an elected democratic form.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents insist on democracy but a qualified, managed one, so they would split on voters choosing badly.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; a managed democracy with a leading state implies representative, party-based channels.

workers-councils.rationale: Opposes soviet-style structures; the state and party of power hold political power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Sovereignty means the nation is governed as one; secession is incompatible with the territorial unity the concept protects.

natural-rulers.rationale: The leading role of the state and elite guidance imply some rule by the more capable; not explicit.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not addressed; adherents condemn revolutions yet back state force.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; stability and development are the stated aims.

separate-church-state.rationale: The state remains formally secular but the concept's backers sought Church support, so adherents lean away from strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not addressed; the framework is secular-constitutional democracy.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state is guardian of sovereignty and keeps core security functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Surkov wanted Russia's global influence restored and tied sovereignty to the army and navy.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Surkov calls promoters of ethnic self-isolation charlatans and presents Russia as a multiethnic nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The concept seeks national unity and justice; class conflict is not its frame.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Aims at justice and welfare but not equal results; inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; a unitary state stresses central authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; Russia as a sovereign great power resists external claims.

civilizational-union.rationale: Surkov calls Russia a half-Western, half-Eastern country that stays within Europe; adherents are split on civilizational blocs.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The concept puts the national community's sovereignty ahead of individual liberal claims; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Sovereign democracy takes no position on environmental ethics, and adherents would not be united on it.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; the aim of national strength implies no population restriction.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Surkov wants a modernising, innovation-driven economy.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Surkov's innovation culture and intellectual economy point to technological change, though he stresses state guidance.

human-enhancement.rationale: Never addressed; a state-guided, tradition-minded outlook is more likely to restrict such freedoms, inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; the concept stresses a leading human state and national political will over automated decision-making.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; implied by state control of information.

restore-past-order.rationale: Surkov frames sovereign democracy as nationalising the future, not restoring a lost order; the Soviet past is not the aim.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Surkov calls for a national ideology of its own, yet the regime stresses pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Not addressed; the movement sought to channel youth activism via state-aligned groups.

means-match-ends.rationale: The concept openly accepts managed means in service of national ends, so an adherent would reject strict matching; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly foreign to a modernising state ideology.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Wholly foreign to the concept's market-and-state economy.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Aims at welfare and justice, not distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: The concept accepts market production and state steering of strategic sectors, not production for use.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The concept has no exploitation theory; it fears oligarchs but not profit as such.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Opposes class dictatorship; claims a democratic national form.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; no support for collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; no Leninist theory of imperialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state-led outlook sees taxation as legitimate state function.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; the state manages public life more broadly than harm prevention.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The concept speaks of the Russian nation as the sovereign subject; individual-only rights are not its frame.

conscription.rationale: Sovereignty tied to the army and navy; conscription is inferred as acceptable.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The concept stresses national political life over exit; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is guardian of the nation, not a business serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Surkov seeks freedom and material welfare together, but this philosophical contrast is not addressed.

media-academia-power.rationale: Surkov's circle distrusted liberal media and foreign-backed intellectuals as shaping politics; the claim is inferred from his attack on those looking West.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Opposes ethnic-nation thinking; Surkov rejects ethnic separatists.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; the leading-state model is party-based but corporatist elements are claimed by some commentators.

total-state.rationale: The concept keeps democratic and market forms while the state leads; it does not call for total direction of culture and economy.

national-rebirth.rationale: Surkov's nationalising the future and restoring Russia's weight after the 1990s imply a national revival.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Surkov says Russians always have matters beyond their borders, but this speaks of influence, so adherents are split on expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Formally rests on a constitutional, electoral order, though informal loyalty networks exist.

bound-labor.rationale: Not part of any modern state ideology.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Surkov's call for a Russian discourse and public philosophy treats what counts as true as shaped by who speaks it; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: The concept emphasises a distinct Russian path and civilisation over universal Western norms; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: The concept speaks of a single national future and justice for Russia, which fits a unified common good; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The concept says nothing about Israel and adherents have no shared view.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Russia's compatriots policy later stressed returning co-nationals; the 2006 sources do not discuss it, so this is an inference.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not relevant for Russian, which is already the state language; no stated view.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed; a leading state and managed public sphere imply top-down management.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; the state keeps its social role.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal caution fits the post-1990s stability aim; no source states a position.

economic-freedom.rationale: The concept subordinates private economic power to state aims, so political freedom is not tied to economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: The concept rests on state institutions and the dominant party rather than rulers' moral example; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Power is to be elected, constituted and directed solely by the Russian nation, a statement of national self-rule.

force-without-un.rationale: The concept claims a right to limit international law's influence, which supports acting without UN approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The concept's backers courted the Church and call Russia culturally rooted in wholeness, so pure reason is not elevated; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare aims are framed for the citizens of the nation; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not discussed; a state-order outlook with a growth aim implies work conditions on benefits, inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: The concept stresses national unity and justice over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Culture as destiny and national tradition rank high; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Surkov distinguishes Western adversaries from partners and resists subjugation, but no common front of dominated countries is stated.

workers-nation.rationale: National unity is the frame, not national working-class organisation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The conservative cultural line later attached to the regime favours traditional roles; the 2006 texts do not address it.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Conflicts with the multiethnic nation Surkov describes.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Presents the state as guardian of the nation, not a class tool.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; a multiethnic frame and a national culture emphasis pull in opposite directions.

elite-replacement.rationale: Never addressed by the concept; a conspiracy view is not part of its programme.

proportional-representation.rationale: The regime used PR with a 7% threshold; Gorbachev criticised that change, but adherents defend it, so no firm line.

national-mission.rationale: Surkov seeks justice for Russia in the world and a Russian path, not a mission to spread its government to others.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed; implied by conservative cultural line.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Adherents defend the leading elite and attack oligarchs and liberals instead.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not part of the concept and out of keeping with its pronatal national aims.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; a security-first state resists such accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The concept gives the state a society-forming leading role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Conflicts with the multiethnic nation Surkov describes.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Surkov declares justice for every person in Russia; legal equality is not elaborated.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed; adherents see the state as a historic nation.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A unitary state with a single law for all citizens is implied; not discussed in the sources.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a formally secular but Orthodox-friendly state.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Russia is a multiethnic state including Muslim and other communities, so the concept has no such religious ban.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The regime's backers supported more Church presence in public life, so a ban on religious instruction is unlikely; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The concept sees hostile external pressure and wants a strong state to resist it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Sovereign democracy claims the nation elects and directs its government, so legitimacy rests on consent, though managed.

trade-surplus.rationale: A resource-exporting, sovereignty-minded state favours running trade surpluses; no source states it.

population-transfer.rationale: Contrary to a multiethnic nation claimed by Surkov.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The state holds force as guardian of sovereignty.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Surkov stresses competitiveness among nations, yet no view of struggle as the engine of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The regime restricts parties and Surkov targets nationalists and oligarchic forces seen as threats; inferred from state practice.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The concept holds that the state may lead and shape political life, which is inconsistent with strict non-domination; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Sources describe a concentrated, leading state; Kirill-style critics of division of power echo it.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The aim is justice for every person, with no priority to the poor stated.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed in the sources, and adherents have no shared view.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The managed public sphere implies tight control of protest and industrial action; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; poverty is blamed on 1990s institutions and oligarchs.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Surkov frames Russia as multiethnic, which implies diversity is no cohesion problem.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Contrary to a managed, party-led system.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: A strong guardian state fits emergency powers; not stated.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not discussed; a state-guided economy with a welfare aim can accept price fixing, inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Surkov monitored media and sought to shape perception; control by the government or ruling party is the practice, though the formal line is democratic.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army is state not party; the dominant party governs without formal party command.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: A sovereignty-first outlook favours restrictive citizenship, though not stated.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; elites in the system are well paid.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: United Russia functions as a disciplined party of power; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Sovereignty is the concept's central term and Surkov rejects subordination to outside bodies.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The strong presidency is central to the system in which Putin leads.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Orthodox Church is episcopal and the concept's backers allied with it; the statement is inferred from that alliance.

clerical-rule.rationale: The state stays civil, merely allied to the Church.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Surkov himself named artistic freedom as the one freedom he admits, but the regime later pressed moral limits; split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The system was built around Putin's continued leadership; not stated in the sources.

recall-officials.rationale: Not addressed; managed institutions imply no.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Surkov wanted Russia influential and partnering with friendly states; ending alliances is not stated.

people-in-arms.rationale: Sovereignty linked to an army and navy under the state.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed; Surkov refers to matters beyond borders only generally.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not discussed; adherents would not share a view.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The concept contrasts the Russian nation with intellectuals looking to the West; inferred from Surkov's attack on them.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The concept stresses a distinct Russian civilisation; equal-but-different is not clearly stated.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a security-first conservative orientation.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; implied by the conservative cultural line.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; the state curriculum stays science-based.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not discussed; Russia has mixed rules and adherents would be split.

minority-language-support.rationale: Never addressed; a multiethnic frame suggests some support.

religious-exemptions.rationale: A unitary state with one law for all is implied; not discussed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The concept stresses national unity and wholeness.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: A sovereignty-minded state resisting outside financial control would sympathise; not stated, inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Surkov holds that independence needs breaking out of a raw-materials economy and state control of vital sectors.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Never addressed; the concept defends the current constitutional order.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The concept accepts a leading state shaping political life for national development, though framed as democratic.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not discussed; the state's focus is on its own interests and influence, inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Sovereignty tied to the army and navy and to Russian security independence implies an independent deterrent.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The system claims the presidency is popularly elected as part of its democratic form.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed; the state steers the economy.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Sovereignty and territory are central; not stated directly.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Strategic sectors are to serve national aims; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The concept avoids a single verdict on the Soviet past and adherents differ on it.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not discussed; the concept resists outside regulatory demands and prioritises growth, inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed; Surkov separates friendly partners from adversaries.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Rejects external judgement on Russian sovereignty.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The concept's backers sought Church alliance, not curbs.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Never addressed; the president and party are closely linked.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Territorial integrity is part of sovereignty; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not discussed; the state's practice of special arrangements for regions suggests acceptance, inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Never addressed (Russia has a flat tax but the sources do not discuss it).

character-from-environment.rationale: Not discussed; no stated position among adherents.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Formally claims constitutional rule even though practice is criticised.

space-expansion.rationale: A great-power, technology-minded state values space achievements; inferred, not discussed.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not discussed; the system blends a strong president with weak parliament, but no theory is stated.

leader-cult.rationale: Commentary notes cult-like elevation of Putin through the movement Nashi; the concept itself does not state it.

equal-parenting.rationale: The conservative family line implies no equal-time presumption; inferred, not discussed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not applicable to a non-socialist outlook, which opposes class-struggle ideas.

refugee-return.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; no stated view.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Surkov speaks of Russian matters beyond its borders but no territorial claim is stated.

common-currency.rationale: Sovereignty implies national currency; not stated.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Surkov's third-road, Eurasian-leaning rhetoric allows for union among kin peoples; the sources do not state it.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Surkov frames Russia as multiethnic and the tradition of national-cultural autonomy fits that; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Surkov stresses ideas, discourse and a national ideology.

ban-cartels.rationale: The state-led economy tolerates large state-linked concentrations; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: The state steers the economy and would support strategic firms; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The concept claims the nation's will governs and rejects outside constraint; courts are not discussed.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas are a Western-liberal measure unlikely to be accepted; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The concept seeks national economic sovereignty but also integration, partnership and a place within Europe.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The concept resists externally imposed standards.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Contrary to the stance against upheaval.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not discussed; Russia has no titled nobility to abolish, so no view.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Surkov calls for a national discourse and ideology; school history centred on the nation fits.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Not addressed; resists foreign tutelage of Russia, applies the inverse.

patriotic-education.rationale: The movement Nashi and the concept stress patriotic loyalty and a national ideology.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preferences are not part of Russian politics and the multiethnic-nation framing favours equal treatment; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from acceptance of market economy.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Surkov states Russians always have matters beyond their borders and seeks restored global influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Surkov seeks partnership with friendly states and a place in the world economy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not discussed and not part of the concept's frame.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The multiethnic frame and strong state favour limits on discrimination; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Not discussed; adherents claim constitutional democracy but resist outside constraints.

elective-rulers.rationale: The concept claims the nation elects its rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: Contrary to a leading state and dominant party.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The concept stresses stability and fears coups.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The regime has a dominant party in parliament, but the presidency leads; adherents split.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Surkov speaks of justice for all Russians; the duty of the privileged is implied.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The concept calls on the nation's political participation under state leadership; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Surkov himself aims to shape public perception; he would not accept this critique.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Surkov holds all democracies are managed, consistent with consent-shaping but not framed as class.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Surkov warns of a raw-materials appendage role for transnational corporations, but no broad world-system view.

party-own-road.rationale: Not applicable to this ideology; no stated view.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Sovereignty and independence from foreign control are central; inferred for aid.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; inconsistent with the unitary nation.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism features in Russian official memory of the war; not discussed in the 2006 sources, so inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Russian official memory rejects equating communism with fascism; inferred, not in the sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: A nation-centred tradition favours keeping monuments; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: A conservative cultural line favours it; not discussed in the sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no shared view.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Sakwa quotes the claim that democratic forms reflect a country's traditions, political culture and psychology, and the whole concept asserts a Russian path.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Never addressed; the army is tied to sovereignty but a political role is not claimed.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; implied by traditional-values orientation.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Surkov wants state control of vital sectors and warns against transnational corporations capturing Russia.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not discussed; Russian law already allows it and no stated view exists.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Contrary to a managed, leading-party system.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not discussed; the leading-state outlook favours state pensions, inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed; private land was legalised.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Formally yes; the dominant party in parliament means weak real check; no stated view.

single-official-language.rationale: Russian state language practice; not discussed by sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A Western legal doctrine unlikely to be adopted; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Putin-era rhetoric is against interference in other states' internal affairs; adherents would deny it.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not discussed; follows from great-power sphere-of-influence logic.

corporate-influence.rationale: Surkov warns against oligarchic and transnational corporate capture of the state.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The concept's core claim is excluding outside influence on domestic politics, and the state later restricted foreign-funded NGOs; the sources describe the aim, not the law.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not in sources; the regime adopted pronatalism, inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Adherents deny that democracy promotion by outsiders is legitimate; Bush's remark on no special democracy was rejected.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The state is the guardian; obedience is assumed.

non-intervention.rationale: Putin, cited in the sources, said Russia is categorically against using political tools to intervene in its internal affairs.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not part of the concept; Surkov attacks ethnic separatist promoters.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Never addressed; state management of the public sphere.

local-production.rationale: Not discussed; the concept favours national, not local, economic strategy, inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: The concept favours state-led managed organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The concept's outline centres on the right to limit international law's influence over domestic policy.

religious-nation.rationale: Surkov's nation is multiethnic; Orthodox ties are cultural.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Contrary to sovereignty and resisting Western tutelage.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The centralised-state view holds revenue should flow through the centre; inferred from Sakwa's account of centralisation.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not applicable to this ideology; no stated view.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not part of the concept; the Church is an ally.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The concept works within a market economy and wants growth; not discussed, so inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not discussed; a Marxist or feminist claim unlikely to be adopted, inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not discussed; Surkov's multiethnic frame opposes it but the state's practice varies.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Surkov presents Russia as a third way between East and West and a distinct path.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not addressed directly; the concept stresses historic national sovereignty.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Never addressed; adherents split between the state's legal stance and conservative pressure.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Surkov warns against nationalists, oligarchs and foreign-backed forces, but the official line is a managed multiparty democracy; split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not addressed; later laws exist but sources do not discuss.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not discussed; the concept opposes subordination of nations, inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The concept is a managed democracy led by the state, not participatory.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A Western academic theory unlikely to be adopted; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; implied by conservative line.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not discussed; the conservative line opposes it, inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Surkov rejects Western ideological categories in favour of a national ideology; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority is held to come from the Russian nation, though the Church's voice is respected.

social-market-economy.rationale: Surkov's idea blends a market economy with a leading state and social aims; not named.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Sovereignty tied to the army and navy.

rich-first.rationale: Surkov accepted growth first; not stated.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Surkov distinguishes adversaries and partners, but a neutrality line is not stated.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not discussed; the concept accepts conventional banking, inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Resistance to outside economic bodies' influence is central.

property-franchise.rationale: Contrary to the claim that the whole nation directs the government.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim unlikely to be adopted; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The system claims constitutional rule of law; not discussed.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; a leading state channels participation.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The conservative line implies opposition; not discussed in the sources.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Contrary to the alliance with the Church.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The state is guardian of order.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Never addressed; the concept stresses national over individual interest, but markets are accepted.

ban-interest.rationale: Not part of the concept; it works within the standard market economy.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Surkov warns that oil and gas dependence is fragile and wants an intellectual economy, yet the state relies on hydrocarbons; split.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: National economic sovereignty implies limits on foreign control of assets; not stated for land.

defeat-communism.rationale: The concept targets oligarchs and nationalists as threats; communists are not the main foe, and Surkov named them only alongside others.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Surkov warns an oligarchic coup would capture the state and reduce Russia to a raw-materials appendage.

missingStatements.text: Ordinary citizens should be able to elect their leaders, but the state may guide political life so that foreign powers cannot shape the outcome.
missingStatements.rationale: The core of the concept: popular rule directed solely by the nation, guarded from external control (Surkov).
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Surkov's concept and too ambiguous to state neutrally; restrict-foreign-funding and institutions-fit-civilization cover its substance.

missingStatements.text: A country should reject outside assessment of whether its political system counts as democratic.
missingStatements.rationale: The concept demands acceptance of its democratic claim without foreign verification, as critics and the outline note.

notes: Most social-policy answers are low-confidence inferences because the 2006 texts address sovereignty, state role and elites, not social questions. Medvedev disliked the term, so adherents were not fully united.
